source_text: Differentiam vero eius non absurde intellegere possumus, variam pro opportunitate temporum dispensationem. Verbi gratia, hostiae de pecoribus in Vetere Testamento fuerant imperatae. Id tunc implere pertinebat ad reverentiam iussionis; nunc vero indicta eorum dissimulatio ita servit iustitiae praecipienti, ut tunc oblatio serviebat. Modus vero eius est vel status, quod nec cuiquam amplius quam vires patiuntur indicit, vel quod misericordiam non retundit. Qualitas autem eius intellegitur, per quam piis mentibus sapit dulciter. Est igitur procul dubio iustitia, sine qua deitas non est; quae si non esset, Deus non esset; est autem Deus, est itaque sine ambiguitate iustitia. Non est autem aliud quam virtus omnia continens, et restituens suum unicuique, sine fraude, sine gratia. Consistit autem maxime in divinitatis profundo.
pass_a_gloss: But its difference we can understand not absurdly as a varying dispensation according to the opportuneness of times. For example, victims from cattle had been commanded in the Old Testament. To fulfill that then belonged to reverence of the command; but now the enjoined leaving-off of them so serves the commanding justice as then the offering was serving. But its measure or standing is, that it neither enjoins on anyone more than strengths allow, or that it does not beat back mercy. But its quality is understood, through which it tastes sweetly to pious minds. There is therefore without doubt justice, without which deity is not; which if it were not, God would not be; but God is, therefore without ambiguity justice is. But it is nothing other than the virtue holding all things, and restoring his own to each, without deceit, without favor. But it consists most of all in the depth of divinity.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: We may reasonably understand its difference as the varying administration suited to different times. For example, animal sacrifices were commanded in the Old Testament. Performing them then belonged to reverence for the command; now the command to refrain from them serves the justice that gives the command just as offering them did then. Its measure or fixed limit is that it commands no one to do more than that person's strength permits, and that it does not repel mercy. Its quality is understood as that through which it tastes sweet to devout minds. Justice therefore undoubtedly exists; without it there is no divinity. If it did not exist, God would not exist. But God does exist; therefore justice unquestionably exists. It is nothing other than the virtue that embraces all things and restores to each what belongs to that person, without deceit or favoritism. Its chief dwelling is in the depths of divinity.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
